children: Benchmarks closed higher for the fourth consecutive session on Monday, as declining crude oil prices and improving global cues lifted investor confidence, though gains remained selective and the broader market lagged.

The Nifty 50 ended at 23,414.30, up 0.29 per cent, while the Sensex gained 0.76 per cent to close at 74,858.99. The Bank Nifty settled at 56,470. Brent crude slipped below $101 a barrel, easing for the fourth straight session on expectations of a gradual recovery in Saudi oil output. WTI moderated further to the $93–$94 range. The pullback in energy prices offered some near-term relief to markets sensitive to India’s import bill, inflation trajectory and corporate margins.
“Improving sentiment ahead of the upcoming U.S.-China talks, renewed hopes of diplomatic engagement between the US and ” said Vinod Nair, Head of Research, Geojit Investments Limited.

Sectoral performance was uneven. Pharma, healthcare, realty and FMCG were the clear outperformers, each gaining more than 1 per cent, pointing to a rotation toward defensive and domestically oriented plays. Metals and IT ended as the session’s laggards. Among Nifty constituents, Eternal and HCL Tech topped the gainers list, while Bharti Airtel and Adani Ports were the notable drags. In the broader market, however, the Nifty Midcap 100 and Smallcap 100 settled in the red. Within the Nifty 500 universe, 285 stocks ended lower despite the headline index’s advance, reflecting weak market breadth.

Institutional activity provided some support. In the previous session, foreign institutional investors purchased equities worth around ₹599.54 crore, while domestic institutional investors invested ₹1,019.69 crore. However, persistent FII selling remains a near-term headwind even as oil prices ease.

On the currency front, the rupee edged up around 0.11 per cent to 95.81 against the dollar, supported by the recent decline in crude prices. “Sentiment remains cautious as crude prices remain elevated and US-Iran tensions continue to pose risks. Persistent FII selling and concerns over higher US tariffs on Indian exports are also keeping pressure on the rupee. Rupee range can be seen between 95.45–96.15,” said Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst – Commodity and Currency, LKP Securities.
Gold came under mild profit-booking pressure as the Dollar Index climbed above 100. COMEX Gold is seen trading in a range of $4,250–$4,450, with MCX Gold in the ₹1,51,000–₹1,56,000 band.

Market volatility stayed contained, with India VIX slipping to 11.29. The Nifty continues to face resistance in the 23,500–23,600 zone, while 23,300–23,200 remains immediate support. A decisive move above 23,600 would be needed to signal a stronger recovery. On Bank Nifty, the 56,900–57,000 zone coinciding with the 100-day EMA is the key hurdle; a break above 57,000 could open the path to 57,500.

Markets will track crude oil price direction, core sector data, global bond yields and any further developments on the U.S.-Iran diplomatic front. “The earnings cycle appears to be turning positive, coupled with relatively attractive valuations in select pockets of the market, continues to support a constructive medium-term outlook for equities. However, in the near term, geopolitical developments and interest-rate expectations will remain key variables influencing investor behaviour and market direction,” Nair added.

title: Sensex, Nifty rise for fourth straight session as easing crude oil prices lift sentiment
